verses.1: Then, with the darkness having arisen, all those gods and demons, intoxicated with their strength, fought, slaying each other.
verses.2: Then, by the army of gods, only one-tenth of the great Rākṣasa army remained in the battle, while the rest were sent to the abode of Yama.
verses.3: In that dark and chaotic battle, all those gods and Rākṣasas, fighting each other, could not recognize one another.
verses.4: However, Indra, Rāvaṇa, and the mighty Indrajit, these three, did not fall into delusion in that battle enveloped by a net of darkness.
verses.5: Seeing his entire army destroyed in an instant, Rāvaṇa indeed became intensely angry and let out a great roar.
verses.6: In his anger, the formidable Rāvaṇa spoke to his charioteer, who was in the chariot, instructing him to drive him through the middle of the enemy's army until its complete destruction.
verses.7: Today, I myself shall lead all these gods to the abode of Yama, in battle, with my valor and very terrible, various weapons.
verses.8: I shall kill Indra, Kubera, Varuna, and Yama, and having completely slain all the gods, I myself shall then stand supreme; therefore, do not despair, but quickly drive my chariot.
verses.9: Indeed, I tell you twice today, take me to the very end (of the journey).
verses.10: This is that region of Nandana where we are now; today, you take me to that place where the Udaya mountain is.
verses.11: Having heard his command, the charioteer then commanded the horses, swift as thought, to proceed directly through the midst of the enemies.
verses.12: Then, Indra, the lord of gods, having understood his (Ravana's) determination, spoke these words to the gods who were also present in the battlefield, while he stood in his chariot.
verses.13: O gods, listen to my words, which seem good to me: this demon Dashagriva should be captured alive.
verses.14: This Ravana, indeed very powerful with his armies and his wind-swift chariot, will advance like an ocean with surging waves on a full moon day.
verses.15: Indeed, it is not possible to kill him today because he is very fearless due to the boon, therefore, let us capture this demon, and be prepared in battle.
verses.16: Just as the three worlds are enjoyed by me after Bali was restrained, similarly, the restraint of this wicked one is pleasing to me.
verses.17: Then, O great king, Indra, leaving Ravana, took up another position and fought, terrifying the Rakshasas in battle.
verses.18: Dashagriva entered from the northern side without retreating, while Shatakratu entered from the southern side.
verses.19: Then, having advanced a hundred yojanas, the lord of Rakshasas covered the entire army of the gods with showers of arrows.
verses.20: Then, seeing his own army routed, Indra, unperturbed, turned back to face Dashanana.
verses.21: In the meantime, the Danavas and Rakshasas, seeing Ravana seized by Indra, let out a cry of "Alas, we are indeed killed!"
verses.22: Then, Indrajit, consumed by extreme rage, mounted his chariot and furiously entered that formidable army.
verses.23: Having entered that great illusion, which was formerly obtained by Indra, Indrajit, greatly agitated, entered and attacked that army.
verses.24: Indrajit, disregarding all other gods, rushed only towards Indra, but the greatly effulgent Mahendra could not see the enemy's son.
verses.25: Even though Indrajit was without armor and being struck there by the exceedingly valiant gods, he did not suffer any harm.
verses.26: Having struck Matali, who was approaching, with excellent arrows, Indrajit then again showered Mahendra with a volley of arrows.
verses.27: Then, Indra abandoned his chariot and dismissed his charioteer, and having mounted Airavata, he searched for Ravana's son.
verses.28: There, Indrajit, powerful with illusion and invisible, moving in the sky, enveloped Indra in illusion and then attacked him with arrows.
verses.29: When Ravana's son knew Indra to be exhausted, he then bound him with illusion and led him around his own army.
verses.30: Having seen the great Indra being led away by force from the great battle by him, all the gods wondered what would happen next.
verses.31: The illusionist Indrajit, the conqueror in battle, is not seen, by whom even the knowledgeable Indra is being led away by force through illusion.
verses.32: At that moment, all the enraged hosts of gods, having defeated Ravana, showered him with torrents of arrows.
verses.33: But Ravana, having encountered the Adityas and Vasus, was then unable to fight in battle, being tormented by his enemies.
verses.34: Seeing his father greatly exhausted and shattered by the blows in battle, Indrajit, standing visible, spoke these words to him.
verses.35: "Come, father, let us go; let this fighting cease, for our victory is known to you; be well and free from distress."
verses.36: "Indeed, this one who is the lord of the army of gods and of the three worlds has been captured by divine power, and thus the gods have been rendered with broken pride."
verses.37: Enjoy the three worlds to your heart's content, having subdued the enemy with your might; why exert yourself in vain here, for today's battle is indeed fruitless.
verses.38: Then, having heard that speech of Indrajit, those hosts of gods ceased from the act of battle and indeed became composed.
verses.39: Then, Ravana, the lord of night-wanderers, having obtained victory and being free from the fever of battle, went joyfully towards his own palace and, having met his son, spoke these words.
verses.40: By those exceedingly mighty valorous deeds, my family's honor has been greatly enhanced, for today, this Indra of incomparable strength and the other gods have indeed been conquered by you.
verses.41: Take Vasava (Indra), place him on the chariot, and you, surrounded by the army, go from here to the city; I also, with my ministers, will quickly follow behind you as you go.
verses.42: Then, the valiant son of Ravana, Indrajit, having captured the lord of the gods along with his vehicles and surrounded by his army, returned to his own abode and dismissed the Rakshasas who had fought the battle.
